correctness.rationale: For exact rational P and stationary pi, two distinct-symbol words 21 and 23 are prime and have measures 1/12 and 1/9. Punctured transition matrices have exact characteristic polynomials ((10z-7)(20z²-12z-5))/200 and z³-(13/10)z²+(21/50)z-3/50. First spectral radius=(3+sqrt(34))/10<9/10; second polynomial is -3/500 at 9/10 and 3/50 at 1, hence has a positive eigenvalue above 9/10. Finite survival equals pi B^n 1, and primitive nonnegative Perron--Frobenius asymptotics give rho=-log r(B). Two-state stationary flow balance makes any strict length-two prime hole-measure order impossible.

An exact 3x3 rational Markov matrix produces a strict counterexample satisfying both prime conditions, beyond Bernoulli product-measure theorems. Targeted literature searches and semantic research-index comparisons found no equivalent, subject to unindexed-literature and later-journal-full-text risk.

value.rationale: The claimed universal conjecture is substantive: it attempts to extend Bernoulli prime-word escape-rate monotonicity to stationary Markov shifts. A three-symbol rational counterexample resolves that yes/no question negatively at the first nontrivial word length, with an exact spectral certificate and alphabet-size sharpness. It isolates transition dependence rather than word-overlap or unequal lengths as the obstruction; this is not a routine numerical observation or known-table recalculation.
